Here's a regex that matches an ISO 8601 calendar date (`YYYY-MM-DD`):

```regex
^\d{4}-(0[1-9]|1[0-2])-(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])$
```

- `\d{4}` matches the four-digit year.
- `(0[1-9]|1[0-2])` matches the month, 01–12.
- `(0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])` matches the day, 01–31.
- `^` and `$` anchor the match to the whole string. To find dates inside longer text, swap them for `\b`.

This checks the format and the ranges for month and day. It doesn't check that the day exists in that month, so `2026-02-31` still matches. A regex can't handle that case cleanly, particularly with leap years, so use a date parser for it.
